audit.whatIsWrong: The entire FULL layer misspells Kled's Q as 'Beartrap on a Rope'. Riot's name is 'Bear Trap on a Rope' (two words). It appears wrong in tldr, winCon, enemyWin, ahead, loading, phases[3].why, breakdown.early/mid/cooldowns/trading/spikes/feeding/difficulty and dosFull. The CONTENT layer already spells it correctly, so the file contradicts itself.
audit.why: Data Dragon gives 'Bear Trap on a Rope'. The packet's name checker only inspected the content layer, so it never flagged this — it reported two content-layer suspects that are both false positives instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three separate strings claim Fury of the Sands heals Nasus: content.mid ('your Fury of the Sands heals through one committed all-in'), content.whys[4] ('your Fury of the Sands heals one all-in') and content.spikes[2].text ('your ult heals through it').
audit.why: Fury of the Sands grants bonus Health, Attack Range, bonus Armor and Magic Resistance, damages nearby enemies and reduces Siphoning Strike's cooldown. It does not heal. Nasus's only sustain is Soul Eater life steal on basic attacks, which does not apply to R's aura damage. A player told 'my ult heals me' will hold a fight one second too long and die.
audit.corrected: Fury of the Sands tanks the all-in on bonus health and resists — it does not heal you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere states that Bear Trap on a Rope's yank is conditional. Both layers treat the hook as 'if it lands, you are pulled'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'If shackled for a short duration, the target takes additional physical damage and is yanked toward Kled.' Getting hit is not the punish — staying leashed is. Breaking the tether by walking out of range before it completes denies both the yank AND the bonus physical damage. This is the single most useful piece of tech for the losing side of a 43.85% matchup and it is completely absent.
audit.corrected: Bear Trap on a Rope only yanks and deals its bonus damage if the leash survives its duration — walk out and it does neither.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer gives an ultimate cooldown comparison, and content.whys[4]/spikes[2] frame level 6 as pure Kled dominance.
audit.why: Chaaaaaaaarge!!! is 140/125/110s. Fury of the Sands is 120/100/80s. Nasus's ultimate is up for meaningfully more of the game at every rank — that is the structural reason a lane he loses 1-6 still converts, and it tells the player which fights are actually free.
audit.corrected: Chaaaaaaaarge!!! 140/125/110 vs Fury of the Sands 120/100/80 — your ult out-cycles his at every rank.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns is a single generic line — 'His engage hook. Dodge it. Track it before every engage.' — with no cooldown, no range and no punish window.
audit.why: Bear Trap on a Rope is 11/10/9/8/7s at 800 range. That is a real, trackable window and it is the only period in which Nasus can step up to last-hit safely before level 6.
audit.corrected: Bear Trap on a Rope: 11/10/9/8/7s, 800 range.

audit.why: content.wants.you[1] already carries the key trading rule — Wither's attack-speed decay lands directly on Violent Tendencies' four-attack burst window. That is the correct read and it is stated precisely, so I left it alone.

43.85% over 244 games. The content layer's level chart (Kled 1-6, Nasus at 2+ items) is an honest match for a number that low, and full.phases agrees except at stages 4 and 5 where it hands Nasus the item stages a little early.

notes: Two packet suspectNames for this matchup ('Stack Violent Tendencies', 'Siphoning Strikes') are FALSE POSITIVES — correct names with a prefix or a plural. The real name defect is in the FULL layer, which the packet did not scan: 'Beartrap on a Rope' should be 'Bear Trap on a Rope' in 14 places. Separately, the claim that Fury of the Sands heals appears three times in the content layer and is wrong — R gives bonus health, resists, range, aura damage and Q cooldown reduction, no healing. That wording is template boilerplate, so it is very likely repeated across many other Nasus matchups and probably across other champions' files; worth a global grep for 'ult heals' / 'Fury of the Sands heals' before the next run.
